Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). This is not the researcher's first guess, and a later guess has to be the fruit of what was learned since the earlier ones. The records marked NEW are what it says it learned from. Say in your reasoning what they show that the earlier guesses did not have, and ask: would the researcher have made this same guess without them? If yes, the citation is for form only and the defect is not_from_what_was_learned.

THE SESSION'S EARLIER GUESSES AND HYPOTHESES:
  [Y1] guess: UDP fills the FIFO queue and tail-drops TCP packets, preventing TCP from getting ACKs and making progress.
  [Y2] guess: The three retransmissions are connection-establishment retries that are dropped, so TCP never sends payload.
  [Y3] guess: TCP's zero goodput is caused by TCP/receiver behavior rather than queue length, so changing queue length alone will not help.
  [Y4] guess: TcpBbr's bandwidth probing can obtain some TCP bandwidth under this UDP load where Cubic cannot.
  [Y5] guess: The larger FIFO admits or retains some TCP segments long enough to be acknowledged, so TCP changes from no ACK progress to occasional ACK/retransmission progress.
  [Y6] guess: TCP enters persistent timeout with cwnd=1 (one MSS, 1448 bytes) during the 1448 interval; the three retransmissions are dropped timeout retries, not payload progress.
  [Y7] guess: The 1.0 ms RTT is an early handshake or initial ACK sample; later TCP segments are tail-dropped, so TCP enters persistent timeout with one-MSS cwnd and RTO doubling to 8000 ms, preventing payload delivery.
  [Y8] guess: The larger FIFO admits or retains multiple TCP segments, producing delayed ACK samples and queueing RTT, so TCP can keep inflight above one MSS and avoids the deepest persistent timeout.
  [Y9] guess: The FIFO's shared tail-drop service, not only its length, starves TCP under UDP overload; a scheduler giving each flow a share of l1 should raise TCP goodput.
  [Y10] guess: Since G17 sent H5 back with no accepted cause, the remaining mechanism is that at q1000 Bbr's bandwidth probing uses RTT samples to pace and avoid tail drops, so TcpBbr exceeds Cubic's 5792 bps by more than 1%.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: l1.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); tcp.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, TcpBic, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

findings.text: E6 q500_cubic r009 records tcp_goodput_bps=1158 while E6 q1000_cubic r003 records tcp_goodput_bps=5792, and the records do not explain how the queue-length change affects TCP goodput.
findings.name: Queue length goodput gap

shown:
THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: l1.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); tcp.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, TcpBic, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE RESULT the guess is about: E5 showed q1000 Bbr tcp_goodput_bps=4634 and tcp_rto_max=4000.0, while q1000 NewReno/Vegas/Bic tcp_goodput_bps=0 and tcp_rto_max=8000.0; with E3/E4, q100 Cubic/Bbr tcp_goodput_bps=0 while q1000 Cubic/Bbr are 5792 and 4634 bps.
THE GUESS of why it came out so: A larger FIFO gives TCP segments more chances to survive UDP tail-drop, so the largest allowed queue length is best for TCP goodput.
THE HYPOTHESIS H9: With TcpCubic, l1.queue.length=500 gives tcp_goodput_bps no more than 1% above l1.queue.length=1000.
DECISION RULE: tcp_goodput_bps@q500_cubic <= tcp_goodput_bps@q1000_cubic * 1.01

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. The defects: none: no defect; not_in_the_records: the result the guess starts from is not what the cited records show; repeats: the guess says again, in other words, what an earlier guess or hypothesis already said, and that one has its ruling; ignores_a_ruling: the guess goes on as if a ruling against it had not been given: it does not say what is different now; not_from_what_was_learned: the guess does not come from the newer records it cites: it would be the same guess without them; no_cause: the guess says that something makes no difference, or that nothing happens, without naming what in the system would make it so. A guess may be wrong and still be sound here: you judge whether it starts from what was measured and adds something, not whether it is true. A guess that takes up an earlier one with a stated difference (another cause, another range, a reason why the earlier test was not fair) is not a repetition. This is not the researcher's first guess, and a later guess has to be the fruit of what was learned since the earlier ones. The records marked NEW are what it says it learned from. Say in your reasoning what they show that the earlier guesses did not have, and ask: would the researcher have made this same guess without them? If yes, the citation is for form only and the defect is not_from_what_was_learned.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: l1.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); tcp.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, TcpBic, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE RESULT the guess is about: At q250, TcpBbr r013 records tcp_goodput_bps=3475, tcp_retrans=64, tcp_inflight max=27512, and tcp_rto max=4000, while TcpCubic r010 records 5792 bps, 15 retrans, and cwnd peaks near 43440.
THE GUESS of why it came out so: Bbr's probe bursts are tail-dropped by the smaller q250 FIFO, producing more retransmissions and a lower acknowledged bandwidth estimate, while Cubic's loss-based single-MSS bursts survive the same UDP drop phase.
THE HYPOTHESIS H16: With l1.queue.length=250, TcpBbr records lower tcp_inflight max and higher tcp_retrans than TcpCubic.
DECISION RULE: inflight_max@q250_bbr < inflight_max@q250_cubic AND tcp_retrans@q250_bbr > tcp_retrans@q250_cubic

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). answer.correct_why: If the tested pacing-drop cause is true, q250 Bbr should have lower inflight and higher retransmissions than q1000 Bbr, so the rule holds; if Y32 is true, queue length only caps the initial burst and the later regime is the same, so the rule should not show this systematic lower-inflight higher-retransmission pattern.

THE SYSTEM, in the brief's words: A network of 2 hosts: sender, receiver. Link l1 joins sender and receiver: it carries 1Gbps with a one-way delay of 50us. On sender's side packets wait in one queue of the knob l1.queue.length packets; a packet that arrives when it is full is dropped. Flow udp is UDP from sender to receiver: packets of 1400 bytes at a constant rate (2 Gbps). Flow tcp is TCP from sender to receiver: it always has data to send; its congestion control is the knob tcp.type. A host with more than one link forwards packets. In each simulation the flows start within the first 10 ms, traffic runs for one second that is not measured, and then for duration seconds, over which the outputs are measured.
THE SETTINGS THE RESEARCHER MAY CHANGE: l1.queue.length (4 to 1000, default 100); tcp.type (TcpCubic, TcpNewReno, TcpLinuxReno, TcpBbr, TcpVegas, TcpBic, default TcpCubic)
TOLERANCE: two results that differ by less than 1 % count as equal.

THE RESULT the guess is about: E4 shows q1000 TcpBbr r004 with tcp_goodput_bps=4634, tcp_retrans=20, and l1_drops=911613. E9 shows q250 TcpBbr r013 with tcp_goodput_bps=3475, tcp_retrans=64, and l1_drops=911653, and q250 TcpCubic r010 with tcp_goodput_bps=5792. V10 supports H14: q250 Bbr <= q250 Cubic*1.01. The new cited records therefore show Bbr falling from 4634 bps at q1000 to 3475 bps at q250, and a q250 Bbr/Cubic comparison of 3475 vs 5792; they do not show q1000 Cubic.
THE GUESS of why it came out so: For a pacing sender that keeps many segments in flight, the smaller q250 FIFO tail-drops a larger share of each probe burst (more retransmissions, more drops), so Bbr's acknowledged bandwidth estimate falls; Cubic's higher q250 goodput is consistent with a loss-based single-window sender not depending on those probe-burst acknowledgments in the same way.
THE HYPOTHESIS H15: With TcpBbr, l1.queue.length=250 records lower tcp_inflight max and higher tcp_retrans than l1.queue.length=1000.
DECISION RULE: inflight_max@q250_bbr < inflight_max@q1000_bbr AND tcp_retrans@q250_bbr > tcp_retrans@q1000_bbr

answer.because: The measured values in E11, q250_bbr inflight_max=27512.0 and tcp_retrans=64 versus q1000_bbr inflight_max=30408.0 and tcp_retrans=20, satisfy both parts of the pre-fixed rule in C12, and the test was honest, consistent, and discriminating, so the result supports H15.

honest.why: The test could have failed because E11 newly supplied q1000_bbr inflight_max=30408.0 against the already measured q250_bbr inflight_max=27512.0 from E10/T58, and the strict comparisons in C12 are not thresholds that almost any result passes.

consistent.why: E11 compares only TcpBbr runs at l1.queue.length=250 and 1000, and C12 checks exactly the two quantities named in H15, tcp_inflight max and tcp_retrans.

correct.why: C12 HELD because E11 shows q250_bbr lower inflight_max and higher tcp_retrans than q1000_bbr, which is the pattern expected if the tested pacing-drop guess is true and not the pattern expected if the competing same-later-regime guess is true.

findings.text: E11 shows q250_bbr tcp_inflight max=27512.0 and tcp_retrans=64 versus q1000_bbr tcp_inflight max=30408.0 and tcp_retrans=20, and the records do not explain how the queue-length change produces this Bbr inflight and retransmission pattern.
findings.name: Bbr inflight retrans pattern
